target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (Fm S : Type) [LogicalConnective Fm] [LogicalNeutral Fm] [Entailment S Fm] (𝓢 : S) [Entailment.Cl 𝓢]
    (K F : Fm → Fm) (conF : Fm),
    𝓢 ⊢ K conF 🡒 conF →
    𝓢 ⊢ K conF 🡒 F conF →
    𝓢 ⊢ conF 🡒 ∼F conF →
    𝓢 ⊢ ∼K conF
a_raw: {"translation":"Target is defined to be the following proposition. For every sentence type Fm and system type S, every choice of logical connectives and truth and falsehood constants on Fm, and every provability relation for systems of type S on sentences of type Fm, take any system 𝓢 in S that proves all classical propositional tautologies and is closed under modus ponens. For every pair of functions K and F from Fm to Fm and every sentence conF in Fm: if 𝓢 proves ‘K(conF) implies conF’, then if 𝓢 proves ‘K(conF) implies F(conF)’, then if 𝓢 proves ‘conF implies not F(conF)’, 𝓢 proves ‘not K(conF)’. The conclusion is a proof of a negation, not a claim that 𝓢 fails to prove K(conF). No consistency assumption on 𝓢 or additional property of K or F is required, and conF need not express consistency or have any prescribed relationship to F."}
translation: Target is defined to be the following proposition. For every sentence type Fm and system type S, every choice of logical connectives and truth and falsehood constants on Fm, and every provability relation for systems of type S on sentences of type Fm, take any system 𝓢 in S that proves all classical propositional tautologies and is closed under modus ponens. For every pair of functions K and F from Fm to Fm and every sentence conF in Fm: if 𝓢 proves ‘K(conF) implies conF’, then if 𝓢 proves ‘K(conF) implies F(conF)’, then if 𝓢 proves ‘conF implies not F(conF)’, 𝓢 proves ‘not K(conF)’. The conclusion is a proof of a negation, not a claim that 𝓢 fails to prove K(conF). No consistency assumption on 𝓢 or additional property of K or F is required, and conF need not express consistency or have any prescribed relationship to F.

divergences.description: The TARGET concludes `𝓢 ⊢ ∼K conF`: it is not known that F is consistent. On the usual two-sided reading of “humanly undecidable,” the passage also rules out knowing that F is inconsistent. That would require `𝓢 ⊢ ∼K (∼conF)`, which does not follow from the premises. The printed corollary is not quoted, so the excerpts do not establish whether its literal conclusion is just the one-sided claim.

judgement.summary: The TARGET states the proposed repair exactly: its three provable implications suffice for `𝓢 ⊢ ∼K conF`. The local inclusion premise comes from the stipulated reading of “surpasses,” not from the existence of an F-derivable sentence that is not known.
